name: Park Medi World Ltd
title: Park Medi World Ltd - 544645 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Park Medi World FY26 revenue rose 21% to INR1,679 crore and PAT 27% to INR274 crore, with gross debt cut to INR28 crore.
summary.overview: FY26 was a record year: revenue INR1,679 crore (+21% YoY), EBITDA INR444 crore (+20%, 26% margin) and PAT INR274 crore (+27%, 16% margin). Q4 FY26 revenue was INR460 crore (+30%), with operating EBITDA of INR127 crore (+44%, 28% margin) and PAT of INR77 crore (+47%). The bed network grew 610 beds to 3,610 at March 2026 (3,960 including Panchkula, commissioned 10 April 2026), and management reiterated a target of 5,460 beds by March 2028. Gross debt fell to INR28 crore from INR450 crore, and debtor days fell to 129 from 161.

financial_highlights.metric: Operating EBITDA excl. other income (Q4 FY26)

financial_highlights.change: +7% YoY for FY; Q4 vs INR28,423 in Q4 FY25

segments.name: IPD
segments.commentary: FY26 IPD volume was 95,525 (+18% YoY, highest ever); Q4 FY26 IPD was 25,329 (+29% YoY per the call).

segments.name: OPD
segments.commentary: FY26 OPD volume was about 7.78 lakh (+22% YoY); Q4 FY26 was about 1.88 lakh (+13% YoY). Total patients served about 8.7 lakh in FY26.

segments.name: High-end specialties
segments.commentary: About 56.9% of revenue came from high-end specialties in FY26, up 316 bps YoY. Oncology was about 6.5% of FY26 revenue versus 5% in FY25, and about 8% in Q4 FY26 versus 6% in Q4 FY25.

guidance_outlook: Bed capacity: 850 beds to be added in FY27 (350 Panchkula already commissioned, 200 Narela targeted for Q2 FY27, 300 Kanpur) and about 1,000 in FY28 (400 Gorakhpur, 200 Ambala oncology extension, 150 Mohali, 250 Rohtak Greenfield, which management said comes January 2028). Target 5,460 beds by March 2028 and, between FY28 and FY33, nearly 10,000 beds.

Capex: about INR55 crore planned in FY27 and about INR250 crore in FY28; management cited about INR500 crore total over the next two years. Capex per bed is about INR34 lakh through the 5,460-bed plan.

CGHS rate hike of about 12-15% is expected to add about 7-7.5% to revenue for nine months of FY27. Management's net impact estimate is 5-6% of total revenue. Actual flow-through likely visible after Q1 FY27.
Payor mix is expected to move from about 80:20 (government insurance vs cash/TPA) toward 75:25 and then 70:30 over 12-18 months. Management's end-FY26 target was about 65-70% government insurance.

Agra (commissioned February 2026) is adding about INR5 crore revenue per month, expected to contribute about INR90 crore revenue in FY27 and turn EBITDA positive. Bathinda (250 beds) is running at 65-70% occupancy.
Debtor days are expected to fall below 100 eventually, but management said this will take time; near-term target around four months of government collection cycle.
capex_capacity: Bed network: 3,000 beds at start of FY26, 3,610 at 31 March 2026, 3,960 with Panchkula (350 beds, commissioned 10 April 2026, capex about INR125 crore). Target 5,460 by March 2028.

Two FY26 additions: Bathinda 250 beds (acquired, Punjab) and Agra 360 beds (UP entry, commissioned February 2026). Narela, Delhi (200 beds, IBC acquisition): total capex about INR80 crore, of which INR55 crore spent. Kanpur (300 beds): about INR30 crore to invest.

Greenfield break-even takes 12-15 months and full recovery 2.5-3 years, per management. Acquired assets' EBITDA break-even is about 3-3.5 years on a weighted average basis; acquisition investment recovered through revenue in roughly 11 months.
Liquidity: FDs of about INR314 crore, about INR100 crore in bank, and INR135 crore non-current FDs at 31 March 2026. Management expects only a small debt raise if any.
demand_pricing: Management says ARPOB is kept in the affordable range and is one of several profitability drivers; expenses should be benchmarked to revenue, not ARPOB alone.
Demand described as strong across Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities, with patients who previously travelled to metros now treated locally.

Collections are described as close to 100% by management. Government (central) accounts for 92% of debtors; government bills are cleared in about three months, and management is seeking to shorten this.
Disallowance on government revenue stayed at about 9% in Q4 FY26.
Oncology is being expanded across all 16 hospitals (medical and surgical), with radiation oncology in three hospitals.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 margin expansion, seasonality, CGHS or case mix?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said mainly higher occupancy at existing hospitals; Agra began operations in February 2026 and Bathinda in May (per CFO), so new units did not drive Q4 margins.

qa_highlights.question: Provision for receivables at FY26 end?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the provision made at 31 March 2026 is close to INR200 crore under Ind AS.

qa_highlights.question: Cost and break-even profile of Greenfield and acquired hospitals?
qa_highlights.answer: Greenfield EBITDA break-even in 12-15 months, with recovery over 2.5-3 years. Brownfield units such as Bathinda were said to turn PAT-positive within the first month. Acquisitions were said to recover investment via revenue in about 11 months.

qa_highlights.question: How much CGHS benefit flows into FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 7-7.5% uplift for nine months of FY27 and a net impact of 5-6% of revenue after mix, largely flowing to revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why is standalone revenue down QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Bathinda was operated under O&M by Park Medi World until it became a subsidiary on 5 January 2026; consolidated revenue is unaffected.

qa_highlights.question: Is capex or debt constraining growth beyond FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth is not being curbed. Capex needs are funded internally, with debt possible for large acquisitions, and it targets about 10,000 beds between FY28 and FY33.

qa_highlights.question: Doctor attrition and incentives?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said consultant attrition is among the lowest, citing clinicians not being measured on volume. Bonuses go to clinicians above the 75th percentile on patient satisfaction and clinical outcomes.

risks_watch: Receivables: 92% of debtors are central government; collection timing and the roughly INR200 crore provision are key to working capital.
Payor mix shift toward government insurance and CGHS rates, with net impact of 5-6% of revenue, depends on implementation timing after Q1 FY27.
Execution of 1,500 beds by March 2028, including Narela (Q2 FY27) and Kanpur; Greenfield ramp-ups carry a 12-15 month loss-making period.
Cost inflation (doctor salaries, consumables) versus ARPOB growth of about 7%; management asked analysts to benchmark costs to revenue rather than ARPOB.
Oncology drug pricing under CGHS: management said it supplied cancer drugs at minimal profit under negotiated vendor rates.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, capex efficiency and the 5,460-bed target. Evasive on cluster-level ARPOB and occupancy data, which management deferred to a post-call release, and on the reason for the ~INR200 crore receivables provision.
key_quotes: FY'26 has been the most defining year in our company's history.
This gives us full funding visibility of our stated growth plan to reach 5,460 bed capacity by March 28.
We are not curbing our growth at all.
we are not targeting the payor mix per se since the beginning of our endeavor.

growth.why: Management targets 5,460 beds by March 2028 with 1,500 beds under execution and capex of about INR500 crore over two years, and cites CGHS rate hike (net 5-6% of revenue) and Agra adding about INR90 crore in FY27; no explicit consolidated revenue growth % guided, and Q4 revenue grew 30% YoY.
